Marathon Petroleum rose 1.94% today to close at $421.96, extending a sharp nine-day rally that has lifted the stock nearly 9% since early September. The immediate driver appears to be a broader energy market dynamic: while oil prices fell on Friday as Saudi Arabia signaled increased crude supply to offset Houthi disruptions and regional tensions, U.S. refineries are running at 96.8% capacity utilization with gasoline and diesel inventories remaining lean. For a refiner, tighter product supplies relative to crude availability can improve profit margins on fuel production, even as crude prices moderate.

The stock's sustained momentum over the past week also reflects the backdrop of elevated energy prices — U.S. crude is trading at $107 per barrel while global crude sits at $130.80 — alongside real operational stress on the transportation sector from record diesel costs. A refiner benefits when fuel demand remains firm despite price spikes, particularly when their own inventory positions are tight relative to the broader market.
